notes: 'A Psalm' is the only added material: the Hebrew superscription writes only לְדָוִד, so the two words stand together doing one office and form a single added unit headed on 'Psalm' (rule 2). The ASV italics corroborate but did not decide it (rule 7).

s011 (זָמַר) keeps its head on 'sing' rather than on 'praises': 'sing' is not a light verb and alone writes the singing, so rule 44's light-verb clause does not move the head. The competing reading is named in that unit's note under rule 8.

The supplied 'unto' of s011 is placed by rule 44's supplied-preposition clause, whose object here is the verbal suffix s012 — that rule states expressly that the object so reached may be a suffix rather than a noun, and the suffix keeps only 'thee' under rule 18.
s010 אֱלֹהִים carries no segmented article, so the written 'the' is a supplied determiner joining the noun's unit under rule 15, never the head.
